title: TachogrApp — Feasibility Study and Cost Analysis of Developing a Certified Application to be used as a Tachograph
description: The main objective of the study is to assess the feasibility of developing and deploying a smart device, such as a smartphone or a tablet, to be used as smart tachograph. The contractor must get an insight of all the aspects that make of the smart tachograph an outstanding device for the purpose of enforcement of a broad spectrum of the EU legal provisions in road transport, assess the equivalences between the tachograph and a smart device and analyse in detail the improvements to be incorporated in the latter so that it can confidently replace a smart tachograph.

title: Supporting Implementation of Interoperability through Better Coordination of Notified Bodies
description: Council Decision 768/2008/EC lays down that the Commission, in cooperation with Member States, must ensure that close cooperation is organised between the notified bodies in order to ensure consistent technical application of the conformity assessment procedures set out in the community harmonisation directives based on the ‘New Approach’ and the ‘Global Approach’. For this purpose, the notified bodies notified for a particular Directive or field must meet with each other to ensure coordination and establish consistent methods which will make certain that their conformity assessment activities are all based on the same agreed principles and produce comparable and reliable results.The purpose of this invitation to tender is to designate the technical secretariat of NB-Rail, the coordination group of notified bodies under Directive 2008/57/EC and Directive (EU) 2016/797 on the interoperability of the rail system within the community.

title: Appointment of Technical Secretariat for the Group of the Notified Bodies under Directive 2010/35/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16.6.2010 on transportable pressure equipment and repealing Council Directives...
description:
The subject matter of the contract is provision of Technical Secretariat services for the Notified Bodies Group for Directive 2010/35/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16.6.2010 on transportable pressure equipment and repealing Council Directives 76/767/EEC, 84/525/EEC, 84/526/EEC, 84/527/EEC and 1999/36/EC (TPED NBG). Directive 2010/35/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council establishes a fully free market for the placing on the market and use of transportable pressure equipment. However, the Directive covers gases transported under pressure, and an arrangement for the exchange of experience between Member States is provided for with regard to notification policy and market surveillance. In order to ensure a level playing field, cooperation of notified bodies within the Directive 2010/35/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council is a key element in the correct application of the legal instrument across the EU and in the associated Member States.
Specialised expertise in the field of transportable pressure equipment and Directive 2008/68/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council (ADR, RID and ADN) is needed.

title: European Urban Mobility Observatory and Support including Web Portal Management, SUMP-Related Activities and Urban Mobility Scoreboard (SUMI — Sustainable Urban Mobility Indicators)
description: ELTIS – the Urban Mobility Observatory: project management, website, newsletter, case studies, mini-clips, tools, statistics, city database, SUMP Platform Coordination Group meetings, SUMP dissemination, development of SUMP guidance documents; translations and design, SUMP coordination/outreach, mapping of cities with a SUMP, organisation of Urban Mobility Days 2022, liaison with EU Climate Pact, urban mobility CSAs, EIP SCC platform, EIT Urban Mobility.Sustainable Urban Mobility Indicators (SUMI) and Benchmarking Tool: Following 2020 pilot project, an indicator set (with data for participating cities) and online benchmarking tool was published on Europa/DG MOVE website. Indicator set and benchmarking tool to be updated annually, aiming for broader outreach to cities. Improvements to the methodology of the indicators, (limited) assistance to participating cities (up to 20 cities/year + ‘secretariat’ hotline), data acquisition fund, validation and publication of the results.

title: Study on the Capacity for Greening of European Sea Ports
description: The study will identify the adverse environmental effects pertaining to ports, the legislation and policies addressing them and which are not addressed and the impediments for ports in pursuing green objectives. It will also present good practices from authorities in terms of policies and incentives aiding in attaining green objectives by ports as well as good practices from ports in pursuing economic development paired with green objectives. The study will also aid in knowledge sharing and identification of the tools in pursuing green objectives so that other ports can adjust and apply them to their own specificities.The study will encompass extensive desk research on legislation, policies, measures and practices on improving environmental factors and impediments in achieving so. It would also require communication and cooperation with MS and industry associations as well as entity stakeholders for obtaining the feedback and proceed to analysis.

The study will also aid in knowledge sharing and identification of the tools in pursuing green objectives so that other ports can adjust and apply them to their own specificities.The study will encompass extensive desk research on legislation, policies, measures and practices on improving environmental factors and impediments in achieving so. It would also require communication and cooperation with MS and industry associations as well as entity stakeholders for obtaining the feedback and proceed to analysis.

title: Technical assistance during the legislative process regarding the Commission’s proposal on the accounting of greenhouse gas emissions of transport services (CountEmissions EU)
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle value procedure. 
Technical assistance to the Commission during the ongoing legislative process for the adoption of the Commission proposal for a Regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council for a harmonised framework for greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions accounting of freight and passenger transport services (CountEmissions EU). 
In the Parliament, TRAN Committee and Plenary votes may be planned for 2024 (presentations of proposal already end 2023), to be followed by trilogues between the three institutions later during next year. During the discussions with the co-legislators, which are expected to continue until Q3 2025, the Commission services get regularly technical questions and request to assess or provide its opinion on various amendment proposals. Furthermore, the Commission services at their own initiative may need to analyse the proposed changes while preparing its negotiation positions. Given the technical nature of the CountEmissions EU proposal, such analysis often requires data collection, analysis and literature research on specific topics. The subject matter of this contract is to make such assistance available at request.

title: Pilot project - Sustainable shared mobility interconnected with public transport in European rural areas (developing the concept of ‘smart rural transport areas’ (SMARTAs)).
description:
The purpose of the tender is to invite a consortium to carry out a pilot project on how to adapt mobility and explore ways to support sustainable shared mobility interconnected with public transport in European rural areas.
 The goals throughout of this pilot project are:
 — provide an open, connected, multimodal and rural environment where ‘smart rural transport areas’ solutions can be tested with target user groups,
 — involve partners at all traffic management levels of different operators (e.g. road, public transport) and authorities (e.g. planning, managing, police, etc.) to work together with industry and public and private service providers aiming at getting a better understanding of the opportunities offered by on-demand services thereby complementing public transport services as well as demonstrate the matureness of digital solutions,
 — getting a better understanding of the evolution of mobility needs in rural areas and how shared use mobility schemes are contributing to addressing those needs.

title: Preparatory Action — User-friendly Information Tool on Urban and Regional Vehicle Access Regulation Schemes
description: In light of the rapid development of UVARs in the EU, an information tool was considered by the European parliament to be a useful instrument for citizens travelling within the EU.Consequently, the general objective of this preparatory action is to foster the real-time information of road users about urban and regional access schemes.The specific objective of this tender is to carry out a pilot project focusing on enabling road users, in particular motorists (i.e. both professional and non-professional drivers) to be fully informed about urban and regional access schemes. This includes working on the needed enablers, i.e. standardisation and data provision for the integration of the information in tools such as apps or navigation devices. It includes also the facilitation of the generation of the necessary information to comply with the single digital gateway regulation.The geographical scope of this pilot shall include at least 4 member states covering around 80 % of existing UV.

title: Technical assistance to DG MOVE during the FuelEU Maritime implementation
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
Technical assistance to the Commission during the ongoing legislative process for the implementation of Regulation 2023/1805, of the European Parliament and of the Council on the use of renewable and low- carbon fuels in maritime transport (FuelEU Maritime Regulation.
Following adoption and publication of the Regulation, on 13 September 2023, the work on implementation is currently underway, encompassing of 1) development of fourteen (delegated and implementing) acts, 2) development of the FuelEU database, 3) organization of preparation workshops and communication initiatives, 4) intensification of the work in the Renewable and Low-Carbon Fuels Alliance (RLCF) and 5) technical exchange and helpdesk support to Member States and stakeholders.
Support is required in the drafting of specific technical elements of secondary legislation and development of examples testing different strategies for compliance with FuelEU. The support must be articulated with ongoing activities related to FuelEU implementation and is envisaged to provide incremental capacity to the Commission in response to technical questions requiring further engineering calculations/modelling and elaboration in the areas of marine engineering, naval-architecture, economics of shipping activities and port operations

title: Security for multimodal passenger transport terminal - best practice toolkit.
description: Multimodal land transport passenger terminals (MMPTs) such as large railway stations need to be protected against a range of security threats. They are complex and have a critical function in the overall multimodal transport system. The security regimes applicable to the various modes of transport are very diverse and are established by different levels of responsibility. This situation can make the task of securing MMPTs very difficult with the consequence of increasing the security vulnerability of both users and employees of these terminals. The project described in this tender specification will aim at mainly developing a working interactive toolkit making the knowledge of security practice gleaned through the PRE-EMPT project available to security managers at multimodal passenger terminals and relevant services e.g. in the police and security services. This toolkit shall be developed to address different contexts within land transport security or even more widely.

title: Mapping study on digital and technical solutions to enable more effective and user-friendly UVARs, while respecting the principle of subsidiarity
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
The justification for the study arises from the provisions of the Smart Mobility Strategy (SSMS) COM (2020) 789 and in specific the 2021 New Urban Mobility Framework (UMF) COM (2021) 811. The SMSS calls for EU and Member States to deliver on citizens’ expectations of cleaner air, less noise and congestion through an improved European framework on urban mobility. Urban Vehicle Access Regulations (UVARs) are essential in this context as a means to address issues of local air quality, congestion and noise caused by urban transport. The UMF calls for an uptake on resolving specific UVAR challenges that risk to adversely affect the internal market as concerns the free movement of persons and goods along the TEN-T network and its urban nodes. The study is explicitly referred to under the action box of UMF chapter 2.7. 
Across Europe, there is a variety of UVAR schemes applied and there is no “one size-fits all approach” for such schemes in view of the specific city challenges the scheme is to respond to. The variety of different schemes, its governance, compliance and enforcement modus-operandi thus poses new challenges for passenger and freight transport which in turn affects and limits the effectiveness of measures taken and leads to complaints by road users. In recent years, the Commission has received an increasing number of complaints from European citizens. Especially during UVAR start-up phases, there is a risk that the haphazard implementation of UVARs jeopardizes public acceptance, creates obstacles to free movement of persons and goods under internal market perspectives and to fair and equal treatment of resident and non-residents (discrimination). Increasing UVAR efficiency under user-friendly compliance and information schemes is thus essential, as is the cross-border data exchange of vehicle and driver data, UVAR digitisation etc.
The study mainly builds on the conclusions and recommendation of the UVAR Exchange Project to be completed in Feb 2023 – and others of relevance such as e.g. the UVAR BOX and Civitas-ReVeAL intervention that ended in theth quarter 2022. The purpose is to map and clarify on digital and technical solutions in order to enable more effective and user-friendly UVARs.

title: Bus and truck drivers from third countries
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
All EU countries are affected by an acute shortage of bus and truck drivers. Professional bus and truck drivers in the EU need to have a certificate of professional competence (CPC). In accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2561, drivers from 3rd countries obtain the necessary qualification in the Member State where the undertaking employing them is established or in the Member State that issued a work permit to them – often by having to follow 280 hours courses and by passing a test. This project contains three tasks: (1) A survey among competent national authorities and other relevant stakeholders in Member States is to be carried out to find out about best practices regarding the employment of third-country drivers; (2) The study looks at the requirements to obtain a driver CPC in 25 third countries each for truck and for bus drivers (12 non-EEA ECMT countries (for truck drivers), 10 non-EU Contracting Parties of the Interbus Agreement (for bus drivers), the 7 countries participating in the EU Talent Partnership Programme and other countries at the choice of the tenderer), compares them with the requirements in the EU in accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2561 and identifies the missing elements. (3) Towards the end of the project, a workshop will be organised in Brussels where the results of the project will be presented to a wider public. Participation in this call for tenders is also open on equal terms to natural and legal persons established in a third country.

title: Appointment of Technical Secretariat to Support the Implementation of Directive 2010/35/EU
description: The subject matter of the contract is provision of technical secretariat services for notified bodies group for Directive 2010/35/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 June 2010 on transportable pressure equipment (TPED NBG). Directive 2010/35/EU establishes a fully free market for the placing on the market and use of transportable pressure equipment. However, the Directive covers gases transported under pressure and an arrangement for the exchange of experience between member states is provided for with regard to notification policy and market surveillance. In order to ensure a level playing field, cooperation of notified bodies within the Directive 2010/35/EU is a key element in the correct application of the legal instrument across the EU and in the associated member states. Specialised expertise in the field of transportable pressure equipment and Directive 2008/68/EC (ADR, RID and ADN) is needed.

title: Green Lanes Support Platform
description:
The purpose of the present tender is to facilitate the operation of an IT business intelligence tool that allows the monitoring of dwell times at the main border crossing points (BCPs) for cargo vehicles along the Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) for road, helping to support the fundamental principle of free movement of goods in the EU, and allowing the Commission to monitor BCP performance, including in the event of traffic disruption (blockades, temporary border controls, environmental disasters, etc.).
The tenderer, either alone or in consortia, must prove technical, organisational and operational capabilities for the creation of an Application Programming Interface (API) enabling the automatic transfer of data to the Commission IT system, as well as experience in the field of fleet management and/or data analytics, ideally related to of on-board vehicle telematics.
The tenderer must prove to have at its disposal the following evidence: At least two similar projects (in scope and complexity) completed in the last five years preceding the deadline for submission of tenders, with a minimum value for each of them of € 75 000, involving the creation of an API; and at least one similar project (in scope and complexity) with a value of EUR 75 000, completed in the last five years preceding the deadline for submission of tenders, involving fleet management and/or data analytics, ideally related to on-board vehicle telematics.
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority's intention to publish a future middle value procedure.

title: Pilot Project - Assessing potential Legal Gaps under UNCLOS and other International and EU frameworks, in and around EU Member State Waters to enhance the Union’s Maritime Strategic Interests
description:
This contract will support a comprehensive legal study focusing on identifying legal and operational gaps that affect the EU’s capacity to monitor, assess, enforce and respond to maritime threats—particularly in international waters surrounding the Union and where there are Ship Reporting Schemes in place. While building on existing tools such as the Directive 2002/59/EC on vessel traffic monitoring and information systems (VTMIS Directive), and the Marine Insurance Directive 2009/20/EC, the project will be expected to examine how broader regulatory, reporting and information-sharing and cooperation mechanisms could be adapted or expanded to enable more effective maritime oversight, enforcement, and coordinated EU responses particularly in relation to non-compliant or “dark/shadow” fleets and evolving geopolitical and safety and security challenges.

The work is expected to identify and assess governance gaps in waters surrounding the EU, through a comprehensive EU legal analysis, taking into account the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and other relevant legal (international) frameworks, guidance, jurisprudence, and best practices concerning rights and obligations, including potential limitations for EU Member States as coastal States and/or port States in relation to flag States. The work will encompass necessary stakeholder consultations, comparative analysis of State practices, including current ship reporting systems and their operations with a view to recommend possible legal measures to strengthen maritime safety, security, and EU strategic interest, by improving monitoring, surveillance, compliance, enforcement and information-sharing at national, EU and international levels.

The final deliverables will consist of a legal brief, a detailed analytical report, and a possible set of recommendations to support future EU policy and actions in this field.

It is recalled that the EU is itself a contracting party to UNCLOS.

title: Framework contract ASSISTANCE TO THE PERFORMANCE REVIEW BOARD AND THE COMMISSION FOR THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PERFORMANCE AND CHARGING SCHEME
description:
For the purpose of the implementation of performance and charging schemes, the Commission is assisted by the Performance Review Board (PRB) established by Regulation (EU) 2024/2803 on the implementation of the Single European Sky (hereinafter the SES2+ Regulation), which is charged with providing an independent and impartial advice to the Commission in accordance with Article 13 of the SES2+. The PRB consists of seven members, including its Chair, who are appointed by the Commission, in accordance with Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/635 . The PRB is in its function supported by the PRB Secretariat, provided by the Commission to assure the necessary analytical, administrative and technical support to the PRB.

The aim is to conclude a single framework contract with one contractor in order to provide support to the PRB and the PRB Secretariat when it comes to the analytical tasks requiring additional and dedicated specialist knowledge on the technical aspects on the implementation of the performance and charging scheme.

Call identifier: EC-MOVE/2025/MVP/0073-EXA

Description: The study will consist of the three following tasks:
•	Task 1: a quantitative assessment of the respective evolution of the market positions of Ukrainian and EU hauliers;
•	Task 2: an evaluation of the causes of the evolution of the market positions of Ukrainian and EU hauliers potentially identified under Task 1, including specifically an analysis as to whether this evolution is the consequence of the impact of the Agreement on the road transport industry or underlying economic trends and/or other market developments;
•	Task 3: the identification of possible remedies to any negative impact possibly identified under Task 2.

title: Book and Claim for sustainable fuels and all transport modes
description: The objective is to assess the need & feasibility of an accountability system for sustainable alternative fuels in the EU transport sector (so called 'Book&Claim', meaning the sustainable alternative fuel is physically used elsewhere but formally associated to another specific transport operation) and will do the following. • Analyse of the existing EU legislative framework, primarily including the Directive 2009/28/EC (RED), Directive 2003/87/EC (EU ETS), Regulation 2023/1804 (Alternative Fuels Infrastructure), Regulation (EU) 2019/631 (CO2 emissions from cars and vans), Regulation 2023/1805 (Fuel EU Maritime) and Regulation 2023/2405 (Re Fuel EU Aviation), with the objective of identifying the viable options for the legally sound set up of a system that would allow 'claiming' the benefits of specific sustainable alternative fuels used elsewhere (both in terms of achievement of specific sustainable alternative fuels targets and in terms of financial benefits deriving from the use of specific sustainable alternative fuels). • Analyse of the existing non-EU legislative framework, primarily assessing any existing barriers for the full deployment (in different non-EU countries) of the established sustainability certification and traceability framework, having as a term of comparison the Renewable Energy Directive III (2018/2001), in non-EU countries. The study will assess barriers stemming from different national legal orders as well as identify other technical barriers resulting from different technical operation system in 3rd countries. This assessment is preliminary to a possible “Book & Claim” mechanisms extended worldwide. The worldwide extension should also assess how the available data under such mechanisms may be integrated or linked to the traceability tool of the Union Database, deployed under article 31a of the Renewable Energy Directive III (2018/2001) in order to avoid double claims or double counting of the same energy units in the EU and in the non-EU countries concerned. The study will prioritise the analyses on those area of the world that have the largest trade volumes with the EU, such as US, North Africa and Singapore. The study will necessitate an in-depth analysis of the legal framework and technologies for the traceability of the rules on a number of non-EU countries, and comparing them with the rules in the EU. • Identify and explore possible ways where an accounting mechanism could facilitate compliance with EU regulations for all actors involved in the production and distribution of sustainable alternative fuels and those actors in the transport sector involved in their use. The scope includes the fuels that available technologies allow to be used in transport, distinguishing by fuel type, including by the feedstock and by the (electric) energy eventually used for its production, the environmental and financial costs of the production and the distribution. • Check the economic benefit of introducing a flexibility mechanism such as the ‘Book&Claim’ and the effects on enhancing or slowing down the deployment of a sustainable alternative fuels production and distribution network in the EU. It will consider if ‘Book&Claim’ can be limited to the EU scope or be extended worldwide, including in the second case a rough estimate if this can favour the development of production and distribution elsewhere than in the EU. Particular attention should be given to the IMO and ICAO ongoing processes of recognition of sustainable fuels.

title: Green Lanes support platform
description: The purpose of the present tender is to develop, operate and maintain an IT solution providing real-time information on crossing time at the main border crossing points (BCPs) for road cargo vehicles, helping to support the fundamental principle of free movement of goods in the EU, and allowing the Commission to monitor BCP performance as a crisis management tool in the event of traffic disruption (blockades, temporary border controls, environmental disasters, etc.). The tenderer, either alone or in consortia, must prove experience in the field of development, operation and maintenance of software and IT platforms as well as experience in the field of fleet management and/or analytics of on-board vehicle telematics data. The tenderer must prove to have at its disposal the following evidence: At least two similar (in scope and complexity) projects completed in the last five years preceding the deadline for submission of tenders, with a minimum value for each of them of € 100 000 and at least one project completed in the last five years preceding the deadline for submission of tenders, involving fleet management and/or analytics of on-board vehicle telematics data. Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority's intention to publish a future middle value procedure.

title: Framework contract for Technical and organisational support to the Digital Transport and Logistics Forum (DTLF)
description: To support the digital transformation of the transport and logistics sector, the Commission established in mid-2015 the Digital Transport and Logistics Forum (DTLF); its mandate was extended in 2018. The DTLF is an expert group bringing together relevant transport, logistics and IT stakeholders, Member States and public authorities with the purpose to discuss technological developments and their translation into a business and administrative environment, promote co-operation, and co-ordinate initiatives and measures aiming at the digitalisation of the transport and logistics sector including the facilitation of data sharing. The Forum defines and recommends possible solutions and areas where EU action would be needed to facilitate the process. The DTLF has initiated and significantly contributed to the work of electronic freight transport information (eFTI) and the respective proposal for Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 and continues its support in the implementation of the eFTI Regulation and the respective implementing and delegated acts. The DTLF further develops the concept of a federated network of data sharing platforms, defining the technical and governance framework for interoperability between individual platforms, databases and registries throughout transport corridors and logistics chains, enabling stakeholders to easily access and exchange data to optimise their business activities and administrative compliance in a trusted and secured environment. The DTLF will therefore be an important source for input to the establishment of the European Mobility Data Space. The contract shall provide organisational and technical support to the future DTLF. Organisational tasks shall include the following: a) organisation, preparation and secretarial assistance during and after meetings, b) document and repository management, c) hosting, management and maintenance of the online collaboration and the DTLF website, d) development and implementation of a communication and dissemination plan, d) organisation of specific workshops and conference(s). Technical tasks shall include: a) provision of technical and scientific expertise, b) support in defining strategic directions and orientations, c) support for the development of technical specifications and standards, d) preparation of discussion papers and reports, e) support in ensuring input to and consistency with the work and results of the DTLF and other initiatives such as the European Mobility Data Space (EMDS), and with and between possible on-going and future projects, e) support in aligning with relevant international initiatives to ensure a global approach where necessary.

title: FWC for Technical support for the development and analysis of IMO regulatory measures and other related EU and international regulations or standards.”.
description:
Decarbonisation of international shipping is high on the agenda of the European Commission, with the Smart and Sustainable Mobility Strategy calling on the IMO to strive for high standards in the field of climate change. IMO adopted a number of measures to reduce GHG emissions from international shipping : the Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII), the Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI) the Ship Energy Efficiency Management Plan (SEEMP), the Data Collection System (DCS), the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI). A GHG Fuel Standard and an economical measure (so called Mid-term measures) must be adopted in 2025 for international shipping to reach the goals set in the revised IMO GHG Strategy (2023). A revision of the CII framework must be further considered at IMO after MEPC 83 and potentially of the EEXI and EEDI frameworks as well. Guidelines will need to be developed to implement the mid-term measures, as well as the SEEMP and the DCS. Additionally, the IMO has adopted and advanced guidelines on the life cycle GHG intensity of marine fuels (LCA Guidelines). Efforts are ongoing to refine and finalize these guidelines, including certification frameworks and addressing technical and sustainability aspects. The LCA framework will support the implementation of Mid Term Measures and need to be further developed to effectively inform and support the regulatory framework. The Commission is expected to continue to play an important role in the development of IMO decarbonization measures in the coming years and this contract will provide technical support for the analysis and development of IMO regulatory measures. The EC is also expected to play a key role in the development of an international framework to ensure the safe use of innovative technologies and alternative fuels as well, as for other international regulations or standards. This contract will provide technical support for analysis and development of such measures. 
In 2023 the EU adopted two key domestic measures for the decarbonisation of shipping. These are the extension of the EU ETS to the maritime sector and the FuelEU Maritime Regulation. Both EU instruments contain review clauses in anticipation of new IMO measures to be adopted in the future and, also, clauses for comprehensive reviews in light the assessment of the functioning of these regulations during the first few years of implementation. The contract shall provide technical support for the analysis and development of the FuelEU Maritime, also in the context of adopted IMO measures. 
The tasks shall include: a) provision of technical, analytical and scientific expertise, b) support in defining strategic directions and orientations, c) support for the development of comparative analysis, and technical analysis, recommendations, specifications, standards and submissions d) preparation of discussion papers and reports, e) support in ensuring input to other initiatives like the European Sustainable Shipping Forum, e) support in aligning with relevant international initiatives to ensure a global approach where necessary.

Both EU instruments contain review clauses in anticipation of new IMO measures to be adopted in the future and, also, clauses for comprehensive reviews in light the assessment of the functioning of these regulations during the first few years of implementation. The contract shall provide technical support for the analysis and development of the FuelEU Maritime, also in the context of adopted IMO measures. 
The tasks shall include: a) provision of technical, analytical and scientific expertise, b) support in defining strategic directions and orientations, c) support for the development of comparative analysis, and technical analysis, recommendations, specifications, standards and submissions d) preparation of discussion papers and reports, e) support in ensuring input to other initiatives like the European Sustainable Shipping Forum, e) support in aligning with relevant international initiatives to ensure a global approach where necessary.

title: Study on seafarer’s fatigue and its relationship with working rosters on ferries
description: The objective of this comprehensive study is to methodically examine the issue of fatigue among seafarers working in various functions and capacities on ferries operating between ports of an EU Member State, between EU Member States and ports between EU and non-EU countries. Recognizing the central role of maritime safety, this research will examine how fatigue, influenced by different working rosters, impacts the well-being, performance, and safety of seafarers. Fatigue among seafarers not only poses a significant threat to their health and safety but also expose the safe operation of ferries, possibly leading to maritime accidents. This study should adopt a holistic approach, considering all elements that contribute to seafarers' fatigue, such as long working hours, insufficient rest periods, irregular shift patterns, and the demanding nature of work onboard on the ship. The primary focus, however, will be on the impact of working rosters on the fatigue levels of seafarers. By analyzing different roster schedules, including those with varying lengths and frequencies of shifts, the study should aim at to identifying patterns and correlations between specific roster configurations and the incidence of fatigue-related symptoms among crew members. The study should integrate biomedical measurements tools to assess the fatigue if possible. The goal of this study is to provide evidence-based insights that can feed policy initiatives, promoting enhanced seafarer well-being and ensure the highest standards of maritime safety. Through these efforts, the study should aim to contribute to a safer and healthier working environment for seafarers on ferries and keep the maritime transport safe.

title: Standardisation of jet fire, pool fire and clogging tests for dry chemical powder used in fixed fire-extinguishing systems
description:
“The development of a jet and pool fire testing standards for fixed dry chemical powder fire-extinguishing systems and a powder clogging test is requested since a fire on board of a ship carrying liquefied gases in bulk may have serious consequences. Moreover, the number of ships using gas as fuel is constantly increasing and specific provisions for fixed dry chemical powder fire-extinguishing systems for ships using gas as fuel will need to be developed.
The International Maritime Organisation (IMO) has been reviewing the Guidelines for the approval of fixed dry chemical powder fire-extinguishing systems for the protection of ships carrying liquefied gases in bulk (see MSC.1/Circ.1315/Rev.1).
During the IMO review it became evident that it would be premature to include new test procedures using jet fire and/or pool fire in the draft amendments to the Guidelines, as no relevant test standards had been developed yet.
The IMO’s SSE7 Sub-Committee therefore noted the need to develop additional realistic test procedures, such as a pool fire test using flammable liquefied gases and a jet fire test; and invited interested parties to engage in any standardization work with a view to their eventual inclusion in the Guidelines.”

title: Assess the modal shift potential to intermodal and multimodal transport in EU.
description:
European Commission intends to launch a medium-value study to identify the theoretical freight modal shift potential in EU. The tasks of the study will be as follows:
1.	The contractors are expected to analyse existing data on road freight transport flows that run in parallel to existing rail, inland waterways and short sea shipping corridors, with an aim to identify the trade lanes with current and future potential for modal shift to multimodal and intermodal transport.
2.	The contractors are expected to identify border areas between Member States, where terminal capacity could be shared and/or developed commonly for two or more Member States.

title: Technical secretariat for national SUMP support programmes
description:
Under the revised TEN-T Regulation, 431 urban nodes on the TEN-T network should adopt a sustainable urban mobility plan and collect and regularly submit to the Commission urban mobility data for all 431 urban nodes. Member States will have to designate a national SUMP contact point to oversee the process and provide support to urban nodes.
The CEF work programme for 2025-2027 includes TA to support Member States to prepare for the above urban nodes requirements. The current action will support the implementation of this TA action.
The action will hire a technical secretariat for 3 years (2025-2027) to establish a network of national SUMP contact points and provide a common platform to stimulate exchange and peer learning, coordinate the activities of MS, identify good practices and offer networking. The secretariat will regularly report to the Commission on the work carried out within the network and offer policy analysis on the challenges and the way forward.
Budget justification: 
The CEF work programme included a a horizontal action for the period 2021-2024 to offer grant support to Member States for the collection of data in support of urban mobility indicators. The total value of the action was EUR 3 million.

title: Implementation of the digitalisation vision for inland waterway transport as part of the European Green Deal
description: Implementation of the digitalisation vision for inland waterway transport as part of the European Green Deal. he Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy underlines the need to increase the use of more sustainable transport modes and indicated that the modal share of inland waterway transport and shortsea shipping should increase by 25% by 2030 and by 50% by 2050. To do so, the NAIADES III Communication indicates that digitalisation and automation are essential to reach these goals and to improve the sustainability, resilience, and competitiveness of inland waterway transport . The Sustainable and Smart Mobility Strategy requires that the transport sector’s emissions are reduced by 90% by 2050. To support achievement of these goals digitalisation is thereby seen as an indispensable driver for the modernisation of the entire transport system, making it seamless and more efficient, increasing the levels of safety, security, reliability, and comfort, whilst improving Europe’s global competitiveness through efficient and resilient logistics chains. One of the objectives set out in the NAIADES III Communication is to make inland waterway transport smarter, i.a. by further advancing the digitalization of the IWT sector. It is imperative for the IWT sector to keep up with digital developments to improve the sector’s competitiveness and ensure that it becomes an active part of broader multimodal chains. Further digitalisation can play a significant role in improving the efficiency and reliability of navigation and traffic management, better integrating inland waterway transport in logistics processes and multimodal chains and reducing the administrative burden and costs of complying with and enforcing legislation. The NAIADES III Communication foresees that the Commission will facilitate the elaboration of a holistic vision for the sector’s digitalisation with the contribution of the Digital Inland Navigation Area, NAIADES Expert Groups In order to meet these digitalisation challenges, the following (draft) vision for a digital inland waterway area by 2025 is put forward: By 2035, inland waterway transport in the European Union is a competitive, innovative connected, cyber secure and digital by default mode of transport which is fully harnessing the potential of digital technologies and emerging solutions, enabling seamless integration with other modes of transport as well as automation, by embracing the latest digital achievements and contributing to a better functioning of the Inland waterway single market. It will help overall time efficient, sustainable transport flows and support other modes to decongest.

title: Observation and analysis of transalpine freight traffic flows by road and by rail
description: The main purpose of the Observatory is to regularly collect data on traffic and transport flows across the Alps and on related issues (e.g. costs, capacity utilisation, quality of service, environmental impact) and to provide a thorough analysis of the developments in order to assist transport policy planning at national and European levels, in particular as regards freight transport by road, by rail and by - accompanied and unaccompanied - combined transport across the Alps. The data coming from various sources will be made comparable and fit for purpose i.e. to serve as basis for decisions taken by the EU-CH Inland Transport Committee.

title: ‘Safe and secure parking places for trucks’.
description: Safe and secure parking places for trucks are needed to ensure socially fair conditions for professional drivers when taking rests. They are also needed to tackle issues such as cargo crime and unintended transport of illegal immigrants. However, safe and secure parking places remain too scarce and the services provided by existing facilities are often insufficient and uncoordinated. The establishment of safe and secure parking places requires some careful reflection on the different requirements to place on the different stakeholders, together with consideration of whether legislative change or other support actions are needed. Against this background, this study will define an action plan for safe and secure parking places with the objective of creating the right framework for authorities and private developers who wish to establish safe and secure parking places.

The framework contract covers studies on all transport modes: aviation, rail transport, road transport, maritime transport and inland navigation. All issues relevant for transport and mobility may be looked into including non-exhaustively: competition, environmental impacts, infrastructure, innovation and research, intelligent transport, internal market, international dimension, investment, logistics, passenger rights, safety, security, social aspects, sustainability.

title: New Mobility Patterns in European Cities
description: Conduct a pan-European survey, combined with related studies, to provide a comprehensive snapshot of mobility patterns in European cities. The survey and related studies should collect information about the new mobility models, the use of collective transport, private conventionally fueled and alternative fueled vehicles, as well as of active modes in European agglomerations. They should also assess the interest of European citizens in shifting to more sustainable transport modes and identify obstacles to their further deployment. The project will be broadly divided into 4 distinct but interrelated tasks.Task 1: a survey on passenger mobility patterns in major European centres;Task 2: a targeted survey on urban logistics;Task 3: Update of TRACCS database.

title: Pilot Project - Enabling Sustainable Management and Development of Inland Ports
description: Inland ports and their activities are crucial to the economic development, their operation can negatively impact the environment. The study will address these environmental impacts, legislation and policy frameworks, and propose environmentally sustainable solutions. It will identify the EU, international legislation and national/regional regulatory. Good practices in implementing green objectives from authorities will be identified. The study will elaborate on the role of inland ports as energy hubs and their circular economy practices. The study will develop environmental and sustainable management systems tools and implement them through pilot projects in some inland ports. It will assess the state of digitalisation of inland ports and identify possible improvements. Ways of adopting inland transport beyond the traditional purposes for urban transport will be assessed. The results will be disseminated with a campaign, website and with the final event.

title: Technical Support for the Railway Interoperability Issues Log Book and Cleanup of National Rules
description: The success of the European Union's TEN-T policy and the EU Railway policy are mutually dependent: upon its finalisation in 2030, the TEN-T network will provide the physical basis for competitive rail services, while the achievement of a single european railway area will ensure that full potential of TEN-T infrastructure can be achieved. The European Rail Union network is still facing too many obstacles to achieve its objective of rail interoperability, particularly when looking at cross-border rail freight. In order to implement a truly single european rail area, a number of operational, technical and administrative barriers to rail interoperability need to be overcome urgently. One of the major hindrances to cross-border rail traffic identified by the Issue Log Book (ILB) initiative is the continued existence of a number of National (Safety) Rules. Major hindrances to cross-border rail traffic have been identified ‘bottom-up’ by the sector in the Issue Log Book related to safety.

title: Supply of electronic data related to worldwide flight schedules for year 2023
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
Electronic data related to worldwide flight schedules for years 2023. 
This data is used to update ICARE database in order to support analysis of air transport supply.

The contract shall provide a supply of electronic data and associated support of information on worldwide flight schedules. The European Commission needs this data to update an internal database on scheduled flights for the year 2023.
The contractor should provide datasets related to worldwide flight schedules for the year 2023 covering four periods of the year as a minimum: one dataset per period consisting of schedules for a single week within a period in question (in January, April, July and October) – including the related reference data.
See provisional data elements related to Datasets for Schedules, Carriers and Locations as proposed in Annex A. As a minimum the fields with their names listed with bold font in the list of Annex A are needed.

title: Assist DG MOVE in developing technical implementation guidance for the development of the eFTI exchange environment, to ensure a timely and coordinated implementation of the eFTI Regulation requirements in all the EU Member States
description:
Please note that this is not a call for tenders but a publication announcing the Contracting authority’s intention to publish a future negotiated low or middle valueprocedure. 
In line with Article 8 of Regulation (EU) 2020/1056 on electronic freight transport information (eFTI), DG MOVE prepared implementation specifications, to be adopted by the Commission in the form of an implementing regulation. These specifications detail the measures to be put in place by the Member States, to comply with their respective requirements under the eFTI Regulation. The implementing regulation has already received positive opinion from the Digital Transport and Trade Facilitation (DTTF) Committee, and is expected to be adopted by the College in May 2024. The implementing regulation contains references to "technical guidance documents" that will provide detailed and non-binding technical documentation, drawn up by the Commission in cooperation with Member States, to support the implementation of the specifications provided in the implementing regulation. The provision of such technical guidance documentation by the Commission is a common good practice to support the implementation of policy initiatives with a highly technical content, and particular as regards the establishment of EU-wide cross-border electronic exchange environments, where harmonised implementation by the Member State is essential to ensure their functioning. Examples include the Union electronic customs systems (under Union Customs Code Regulation (EU) No 952/2013), the Once Only Technical System (under the Single Digital Gateway Regulation (EU) 2018/1724), or the European Maritime Single Window environment (under EMSWe Regulation (EU) 2023/205). With the entry into force of the implementing regulation, expected September 2024, the countdown for the Member States to meet their implementation obligations will start. And many Member States view as essential the availability of the implementation guidance documents as soon as possible as of that date, as that would allow them to more accurately define their procurement requirements and budgetary allocations. The contractor is expected to assist DG MOVE.D1 eFTI team in drawing up these technical guidance documentation, based on preparatory technical documents already developed under a previous external contract supporting the preparation of the eFTI Regulation implementation specifications, but also using their own technical expertise to revise and complete the technical specifications included in those documents. The contractor is also expected to assist the Commission in presenting and discussing the technical documentation with the Member States' experts, and assist with finding agreements on technical solutions that can be cost-effective for all Member States.

title: Observation and Analysis of Transalpine Freight Traffic Flows by Road and Rail
description: The main purpose of the observatory is to regularly collect data on traffic and transport flows across the Alps and on related issues (e.g. costs, capacity utilisation, quality of service, environmental impact) and to provide a thorough analysis of the developments in order to assist transport policy planning at national and European levels, in particular as regards freight transport by road, by rail and by — accompanied and unaccompanied — combined transport across the Alps. The data coming from various sources are to be made comparable and fit for purpose i.e. to serve as a basis for decisions taken by the EU-CH Inland Transport Committee.

title: Study on the opportunities to evolve TAF TSI to exploit synergies with e-enhanced multimodal logistics
description:
A specific technical standard for rail interoperability concerns “telematics application for freight services” (“TAF TSI”).
 The system has so far achieved standardisation and enhancement of exchanges between different rail infrastructure managers and railway undertakings, with very marginal involvement of terminals and therefore of the intermodal / multimodal dimension.
 In the wide framework of e-enhanced multimodal logistics, and digitalisation of transport, several initiatives are being currently proposed by the Commission and/or discussed in the Digital Transport and Logistics Forum. These elements, facilitating multimodal integration, represent a major opportunity for railway (a non-door-to-door model therefore in need of smooth multimodal exchanges); however, delays in rail digitalisation / development of rail-only environments / tools might jeopardize this opportunity and set railways apart from the integration they offer, therefore curbing perspectives for freight transport.

title: “Assessment of infrastructure costs calculation, tolls calculation and variation for heavy goods vehicles in Member States”
description: Directive 1999/62/EC, as amended by Directive 2006/38/EC and by Directive 2011/76/EU, provides the legal Framework for the tolling of heavy goods vehicles in the EU. The Directive stipulates that tolls shall be based on the recovery of infrastructure costs, and, as the case may be, on the recovery of the cost of traffic-base air and/or noise pollution. 6 months before the implementation of new or substantially amended tolling schemes, Member States have to provide the Commission with a detailed description of the new system. A number of Member States are expected to notify the Commission about new or substantially amended tolling schemes in 2018-19. The contractor will assist the Commission in the assessment of these notifications, in accordance with Article 7h(2) of Directive 1999/62/EC.

The toolkit will contain recommended good practices covering both generic aspects of cyber-security and in addition more specific modules related to the needs of each transport mode.

title: Single European Digital Enforcement Area (SEDEA)
description: In order to ensure effective, reliable and consistent monitoring and control of compliance with EU road transport legislation there must be an adequate enforcement mechanism in place. In recognition of the importance of law enforcement, the EU introduced certain minimum requirements for carrying out controls of compliance with the relevant rules during controls at roadside and checks at premises of the road transport undertaking. Despite developments made at national, European and international levels to step up enforcement, the complexity of the rules applicable to highly mobile road transport sector remains a huge challenge. The general objective of the project is to initiate the process of creating a regulatory and technological environment for for checking compliance with the EU road transport rules in the smartest and most efficient possible way, using the potential of the existing and emerging digitalisation, automation and communication technologies.

title: Pan-European road safety awareness campaign
description: The pan-European campaign will test how effectively the Commission can help enhance best practice exchanges between Member States, foster the dissemination of knowledge and expertise and influence results by soft measures whilst fully respecting the principle of subsidiarity. The project will focus on a selected number of Member States, in particular those where road safety requires significant improvements as road safety records are below the EU average. The project will facilitate the exchange of knowledge and good practices between the best performing Member States and those lagging behind. The project's activities will take the form of different twinning exercises covering effective road safety strategies, policies and actions. Among many possible sub-themes however, effective enforcement of traffic rules should be part of the activities targeting each country, given that road users' behaviour is always a crucial part of improving road safety record.
